findings.defect: Staging directories are manipulated by pathname in a potentially writable parent. An attacker can replace a staging directory with a symlink before set_permissions, causing chmod to follow the symlink. rename_noreplace then publishes that symlink, and the function returns success without validating it. This violates both symlink rejection and the prohibition on repairing existing objects.
findings.scenario: Call prepare_socket_dir("/shared/private/sock") where /shared permits another user to rename entries and has no sticky bit. After staging-directory creation, that user renames the staging directory aside and replaces its name with a symlink to an existing file owned by the daemon user. set_permissions changes that file to 0700; rename_noreplace moves the symlink to /shared/private; the function returns Ok even though the socket parent is a symlink.
